title: RAG versus fine-tuning: cost, freshness and traceability

videos.script: Your support assistant tells customers they have fourteen days to return a book. The rule changed in February. {{wrong}} There are two ways to fix it. Retrain the model, or change what it reads. {{two}} Fine-tuning changes the model. It is good at habits, like a format or a tone, and bad at facts. {{habits}} Watch a training set built from the documents. Its second line teaches last year's rule, and nothing marks it. {{dataset}} Retrieval changes what the model reads. Re-embedding the new policy takes under half a second. {{fresh}} Every answer points at its source, so a wrong one can be traced. {{trace}} And deleting a document is deleting rows. A model cannot unlearn that way. {{delete}} Then the bill. Retrieval pays a little on every question. Fine-tuning pays a lot every time the facts change. {{cost}} Knowledge goes in documents. Behaviour can go in the weights. The best systems do both. {{end}}
